cleared.check: Task 2 (L-1213), aarch64: the shipped State::rollback 0x1d98170 with its AccountChange arm 0x1d9826c-0x1d98354, the flags rule 0x1d981c0-0x1d9820c, the not-found arm 0x1d98444-0x1d984a0, the StorageChange, StorageWarmed and TransientStorageChange arms, the account map lookup 0x1d89598 and the slot map lookup 0x1d915f4, run in the a64emu model on real hashbrown tables built in model memory, with the cycle 30 SSTORE segments, State::tstore and State::tload as writers (scripts/acct_a64.py).
cleared.result: No mismatch. With EIP-161 rules on (feature bit 14, seed 2026112731) 500 cases and with them off (seed 2026112732) 500 cases, 17947808 and 18681675 modelled instructions, 726 and 730 table resizes, every account's 96 byte present value (balance, nonce, code hash, code and extension pointers), its flags byte, every storage word, every transient word and every read equal both references: the evm2 rule reference and the pyevm.py World driven with its own snapshot and restore and value rule. Sequences move native value (including to self, zero value and short balance), bump nonces including at 2^64-1, create accounts that did not exist, set code, touch, write storage and transient storage, and revert inner, nested and outer frames up to depth 5. One case in five puts 3, 6 or 10 accounts and slot keys into one probe chain with the same control byte, others add deleted buckets to the chain, and tables grow inside frames, which moves every record the journal later restores. Arc reference counts of code and extension pointers equal the references held after every case, so the arm drops the replaced value and moves the journaled one in, once. The not-found arm ran on 50 entries whose address is not in the map: nothing is inserted, no other account changes, the entry's pointers are released. Coverage: AccountChange arm 50 of 59 instructions (the rest are the drop_slow calls and the path without bit 14, run in the second set), flags rule 19 of 19, not-found arm 16 of 24 (drop_slow calls), account lookup 65 of 65, slot lookup 66 of 66. The binary keeps TOUCHED only for address 0x...03 under bit 14, as state/mod.rs:891-901 says. A first run of the bit 14 set (kept as results/acct_a64_none_f4000_run1.json) had 2 records that differ only from pyevm.py, on accounts whose balance passed 2^256-1: evm2 saturates the receiver (state/mod.rs:775) and pyevm.py does not; the binary agreed with the evm2 rule there, and the rerun leaves such accounts out of the pyevm.py comparison only.

cleared.check: Task 5: planted faults in in-memory copies of the lifted programs, each replacing one to six instructions (or, for commit_on_revert, the harness skipping the rollback a revert status asks for).
cleared.result: Every fault is caught on both architectures. aarch64: wrong_field 67 of 150 (16 by mismatch, 51 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); skip_part 40 of 150 (40 by mismatch, 0 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); skip_present 71 of 150 (52 by mismatch, 19 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); skip_flags 71 of 150 (71 by mismatch, 0 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); touch_inverted 69 of 150 (69 by mismatch, 0 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); acct_probe_short 61 of 150 (0 by mismatch, 61 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); slot_probe_short 62 of 150 (0 by mismatch, 62 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); acct_key_short 5 of 150 (4 by mismatch, 1 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); commit_on_revert 77 of 150 (77 by mismatch, 0 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised). x86_64: wrong_field 59 of 100 (59 by mismatch, 0 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); skip_part 48 of 100 (48 by mismatch, 0 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); skip_present 58 of 100 (40 by mismatch, 18 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); skip_flags 61 of 100 (61 by mismatch, 0 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); touch_inverted 61 of 100 (61 by mismatch, 0 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); acct_probe_short 1 of 100 (0 by mismatch, 1 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); slot_probe_short 26 of 100 (0 by mismatch, 26 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); acct_key_short 2 of 100 (2 by mismatch, 0 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised); commit_on_revert 62 of 100 (62 by mismatch, 0 by a lookup or Arc check the harness raised). The faults are: a restored field read from the wrong journal offset, 16 or all 96 bytes of the present value not written back (a skipped balance and nonce undo), the flags byte not written back, the precompile-3 touch rule inverted, a lookup that gives up after one probe group (account and slot), an account lookup that ignores the last four address bytes, and a commit taken on a revert status. The x86 account probe fault is caught only once in 100 cases, because 16 byte groups overflow rarely with at most 13 accounts in one chain.

cleared.check: Task 3 (L-1207): the CALL family and execute_call_message in both binaries, read from the disassembly and set against evm2 at 35aa3280. aarch64: CALL handler B 0x3b62b20 -> call body 0x42b03e0 -> execute_message 0x42b0fbc -> execute_call_message 0x42b12b0 (execute_create_message 0x42b1568), finish_call_message_run 0x42b5c80, execute_call_precompile 0x42b58d8. x86_64: execute_message 0x4ae9d50, execute_call_message 0x4aea130, finish 0x4aef560, precompile path 0x4aef160.
cleared.result: Both binaries do what the source does, with no Tempo-only branch between checkpoint and commit other than the precompile provider call. Depth check first (depth above initial depth plus 1024 gives CallTooDeep 0x11 with no checkpoint). The checkpoint is the journal length and log length (State+0x30 and +0x48) read before the value transfer. The transfer runs for kinds 0, 2 and 5 (bit mask 0x25: Call, CallCode, StaticCall), not for DelegateCall; a short balance gives OutOfFunds 0x12 with nothing to undo. Then the provider vtable decides precompile or not (aarch64 [evm+0x5d0]+0x38). Empty code gives Stop with full gas. Otherwise run_frame saves and restores the frame checkpoint and finish_call_message_run calls State::rollback when the stop byte is 4 or more, which is every status except Stop 1, Return 2 and SelfDestruct 3 (InstrStop, interpreter/mod.rs:55-130). On the precompile path, Ok gives Return with no rollback unless gas remaining exceeds the limit (then PrecompileOOG 0x23 with rollback); Revert gives 0x10 with its output and a rollback; OutOfGas gives 0x23 and other halts 0x30, both with empty output and a rollback; database and fatal errors roll back and return an error. execute_message (aarch64 0x42b0fbc) also rolls back to its own checkpoint on any host error. In the CALL body the success word pushed is (stop - 1) < 3, gas comes back for the stop mask 0xf000e (success and the four frame-revert codes), refunds merge only when stop is 3 or less, FatalExternalError 0x34 propagates, min(output length, out size) bytes are copied to memory, and the return data buffer is set to the output for every non-fatal stop: the revert data after REVERT, empty after a halt or out of gas. This is call_with in interpreter/instructions/system.rs:307-337.

cleared.check: Task 3: does a TIP-20 transfer made by a precompile inside a frame that later reverts get undone by the same journal, and can a precompile open a path that commits after a revert status.
cleared.result: Yes it is undone, and no such path was found. Tempo's precompile storage provider writes through the evm2 account handle and slot handle (sstore_journal: state.account(), account.storage(), slot.write(), storage/evm.rs:185-211), so every TIP-20 balance write is a StorageChange entry in the journal that execute_call_message's rollback pops. Its own checkpoint and checkpoint_revert call State::checkpoint and State::rollback (storage/evm.rs:743-759), and nested calls from a precompile are refused while any precompile checkpoint is open (storage/evm.rs:677-693), so a precompile cannot commit a callee and then roll back around it. The live run below shows the effect on the deployed PoolManager.

cleared.check: Task 5, live: read-only calls on rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz at block 51033487 (0xa3284c58fcfd48f392cafa32d7b81200f400ca41075c61067b374b127599cdda) on the deployed PoolManager 0x33620f62c5b9b2086dd6b62f4a297a9f30347029 (24,009 bytes, sha256 f017c3da36573b60...). A driver placed by state override unlocks; a helper takes 1,000,000 units of pathUSD (TIP-20 precompile 0x20c0...0000, PoolManager balance 19,999,506,794) to itself and reverts, then the driver reads deltas, NonzeroDeltaCount and four balances, syncs and settles (scripts/live_take_revert.py).
cleared.result: Node and reference (pyevm.py with a minimal token at the token address seeded from the node's balanceOf answers) give the same bytes in every variant: revert equal, kept equal, nested equal, roundtrip equal. In 'revert' and 'nested' the helper's call fails, every delta and the count read zero, the PoolManager still holds 19,999,506,794 and the helpers 0, settle returns 0 and the unlock closes. In 'kept' the helper returns and the unlock reverts with CurrencyNotSettled (0x5212cba1). In 'roundtrip' the driver takes 1,000,000, a helper takes 500,000 and reverts, the driver's delta is -1,000,000 and the helper's 0, the driver sends the tokens back with TIP-20 transfer, settle returns 1,000,000 and the unlock closes. Under a block time of 1796745600 (after T14) run through eth_simulateV1 the four results are the same: revert equal, kept equal, nested equal, roundtrip equal. So take (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297) and the token call it makes (src/types/Currency.sol:60-75) are both undone with the frame, and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364) reads the restored balance.

cleared.check: Task 4: Tempo's TIP-1060 storage credit accounting inside SSTORE for the PoolManager's storage shapes. Source: the SSTORE override (evm/src/instructions.rs:86-139) and sstore_storage_credits (precompiles/src/storage_credits/accounting.rs:110-200). Live: a first write of slot0, ticks -600 and 600 initialised, cleared and initialised again, and the driver's position going from 0 to 10^18, to 0 and back, with and without a helper that adds liquidity and reverts (scripts/live_credit_shapes.py).
cleared.result: The credit path changes neither the stored word nor its journal entry. The PoolManager's own write and its StorageChange entry are made by host().sstore before the accounting runs. The accounting reads and writes only the StorageCredits precompile's slot for the owner and its transient state, through the same journaled host calls, and charges gas. It can stop the instruction only by running out of gas or by a fatal error when the stored credit word does not fit in u64, which no write path produces (credits change by one with saturating u64 arithmetic). A halt rolls back the whole frame, the PoolManager write with it. At the end of a successful transaction settle_storage_credit_refunds (handler/config.rs:444-487) lowers credit balances in the StorageCredits precompile and records a gas refund for the fee payer. It writes no TIP-20 balance of the PoolManager and runs after the last frame, so it cannot move a balance that sync or settle read. Live at block 51033694 (0x165ebf70e7ce292caa51c6ed96a9e484337d416c32cc5be99f61a76f3e493e1f): the reads show slot0 written, both tick words and the position slot set, cleared to zero and set again, and node and pyevm.py, which has no credits, give the same bytes: cycle equal, helper equal. The same under eth_simulateV1 at time 1796745600: cycle equal, helper equal. The SSTORE body's credit code in the binary (aarch64 0x3b563d4) was not lifted; this check rests on the source at a9d6748 and the live comparison.

cleared.check: Writer side of AccountChange entries in evm2 35aa3280: when is the entry recorded and pushed, and can a handle override what a revert restores.
cleared.result: AccountHandle records one snapshot of present and flags before its first mutation and pushes it when the handle is dropped (state/account.rs:286-372). A handle borrows State mutably, so none can be held across a nested call, and every frame's changes land after its checkpoint. override_balance and override_nonce change the live value and the snapshot together (state/account.rs:709-731), so a revert would not undo them; no call to them appears outside tests in the evm2 and Tempo files read here, and the rest of both trees was not searched. On Tempo the native value the arm restores is not an asset the PoolManager can hold: the node refuses value transfers (earlier cycles), so pools on Tempo hold TIP-20 balances, whose undo is the StorageChange arm.

leads.question: Lift the TIP-1060 credit code inside the shipped SSTORE body (aarch64 0x3b563d4, x86_64 0x42a0d20) for the zero-crossing shapes, and the x86 not-found arm of State::rollback, which this cycle read in source and tested live only.
leads.why: The credit code sits between the PoolManager's journaled write and the end of the instruction; a fault there could halt writes that cross zero or corrupt the StorageCredits slot.

leadResults.answer: The AccountChange arm, the flags rule and both hashbrown lookups ran from the shipped code of both v1.19.1 binaries on real tables with colliding control bytes, deleted buckets and growth inside frames. After every inner, nested and outer revert every balance, nonce, code pointer, flags byte, storage word and transient word equals its pre-frame value (aarch64 1,000 cases, x86_64 600), and nine planted faults are caught on each architecture.

Release check: no release after v1.19.1. execute_call_message, finish_call_message_run, the precompile path, execute_message and the CALL body were read in both binaries and match evm2 35aa3280: checkpoint before the transfer, rollback for every stop except Stop, Return and SelfDestruct, the success word is (stop - 1) < 3, return data is the revert output or empty after a halt. The only Tempo-specific step inside the checkpoint is the precompile provider, whose storage writes use the same journal. LOG and the SLOAD database path were not read. The TIP-1060 code was read in source and checked live, not lifted.
